steps.comment: A full party at the level the tower expects, and the three numbers the ending reads back out loud. Nothing below depends on them; they are here so that the run is a plausible one rather than a lone level-one Bram.

The harness, and the reason this file was rewritten. The finale's optional content - clause seven, the materials question, the bounty tiers, the stores-book line - is *made of* Show Text inside Conditional Branch, and the previous version of this scenario tested the finale by deleting every Show Text before running it. Everything it asserted was true and none of it was about a branch, so four shipped endings had nothing standing behind them at all.

So instead of removing the messages, take the blocking out of them: `Game_Message.add` records the line rather than queueing it, and `isBusy` always answers false, so the interpreter runs the whole list start to finish without a key press and without ever opening a window - `hasText()` is false, so `Window_Message` never even tries. What comes back is every line the player would have read, in order, in an array that can be asserted against. The choice fork gets a shim that answers it immediately with `window._pick`, because a choice left unanswered takes *neither* branch: `command402` compares against a `_branch` entry that nothing ever wrote, so both halves are skipped and the run quietly loses a hundred lines.
steps.eval: (function () { window._lines = []; window._pick = 0; Game_Message.prototype.add = function (text) { window._lines.push(text); }; Game_Message.prototype.isBusy = function () { return false; }; const setupChoices = Game_Interpreter.prototype.setupChoices; Game_Interpreter.prototype.setupChoices = function (params) {   setupChoices.call(this, params);   $gameMessage.onChoice(window._pick); }; window.SKIP_SLOW = [301, 354, 230, 221, 222, 223, 225]; window.runFinale = function (skips) {   const skip = new Set(skips);   window._lines = [];   $gameMap._interpreter.setup(     $dataMap.events[2].pages[0].list.filter(c => !skip.has(c.code)), 2); }; window.saw = function (s) { return window._lines.join('\n').indexOf(s) >= 0; }; window.at = function (s) { return window._lines.join('\n').indexOf(s); };})()

steps.comment: Pass A: the plain ending, and the control for all seven that follow. The slow-command skip list is the other half of the trick - with 230, the screen tints and the shakes gone the whole finale executes inside a single frame, because `Game_Interpreter.update` will run a hundred thousand commands before it decides it has frozen. That is what makes eight passes affordable where the old one pass cost twelve hundred frames.

steps.comment: Pass D is the one worth having. Both questions asked, and the Two Hundred flown - which is the state a thorough player finishes in, and the only state in which the game's central joke is on screen. Grimspite says she will never get one off the ground in sight of this place; four hundred lines later the ending reports that she did, and landed next to him. Neither branch knows the other exists and nobody in the game ever reconciles them. Nothing else asserts that the two halves can both be shown in one playthrough, and if a later edit ever makes them exclusive the joke is gone with no other symptom.

The crate can be spent two ways and this line is the only place in the game that ever says which way it went, so it is also the only thing that can tell a player who blew up the Dark Lord that the works found out. `item_one_throne` proves the scene sets switch 71; this proves the ending reads it.

steps.comment: Pass H is the original scenario, unchanged in what it asserts and now run last. Only the battles come out of the list this time: the waits, the tints, the shake and the return to the title screen all run at their real length, so this is the pass that says the finale gets to the end of itself rather than the pass that says what it printed on the way. Two boss phases would cost an hour of software-rendered animation here and would only re-test what battle_mook and balance.py already cover. It also throws away the receipts the seven fast passes each gained on their way past, because a check that reads 8 is not asserting that Grimspite signs one over, it is counting how many times this file has run the scene.
